verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe recurring scheduled runs ("morning PR reviews, overnight CI failure analysis, weekly dependency audits") and several trigger paths: automatic review on every PR, CI via GitHub Actions/GitLab, Slack mentions that return a pull request, and MCP channels reacting to webhook events while the user is away. The sandboxed Bash tool supports unattended execution. Community complaints about output quality do not contradict that the scheduling and trigger features exist. Missing for 10: in-depth setup docs for schedules and always-on hosting (cron configuration, cloud vs. local persistence), and independent hands-on corroboration that scheduled or triggered agents autonomously fix code end-to-end.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Run Claude on a schedule to automate work that repeats: morning PR reviews, overnight CI failure analysis, weekly dependency audits, or syncing docs after PRs merge.
schedule recurring tasks, and kick off cloud sessions.
